title: Hypercontractivity for symmetric discrete laws
statement: Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space and let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be measurable and symmetric in distribution, with a finite set of values supporting $X$ almost everywhere and each value in that set having probability at least $\lambda$. Suppose $q>2$ and $0<\lambda\le1$, and put $\rho=\lambda^{1/2-1/q}/\sqrt{q-1}$. Then $X$ is $(2,\mathrm{ENNReal}(q),\rho)$-hypercontractive and $(\mathrm{ENNReal}(q/(q-1)),2,\rho)$-hypercontractive; here hypercontractivity includes the exponent and parameter constraints, the required integrability, and the affine norm inequality for every pair of real scalars.
hypotheses_covered: $X$ is supported almost everywhere on a finite set whose values each have probability at least $\lambda$
replaced: Let $q>2$, $0<\lambda\le1$, and let measurable $X$ have a symmetric law on a probability space, supported almost surely on a finite set whose atoms each have mass at least $\lambda$. Setting $\rho=\lambda^{1/2-1/q}/\sqrt{q-1}$, both $H_{2,q,\rho}(X)$ and $H_{q/(q-1),2,\rho}(X)$ hold. Write $H_{p,q,\rho}(X)$ for $1\le p\le q\le\infty$, $0\le\rho<1$, $X\in L^q(\mu)$, and $\|a+\rho bX\|_q\le\|a+bX\|_p$ for all $a,b\in\bbr$.
